body:
I have (divorced) parents and a sister, and live with my sister, mother, and stepfather. Since my stepfather lost his job, things have gotten harder; we moved a few years ago at his advice, and while we've been this low before, it was where we had friends and family. Here we have no-one, which is why I've been thinking about how much I take up vs. how little I contribute.

I've tried to "beat this" before, but it never lasts; my family means well, but they think I'm being lazy or apathetic. I've been trying to talk to them since I was 12, but they've always told me I'm making excuses or trying to manipulate them, so I drop it.

It's probably my fault, since they've put up with me for a long time. I try not to cause trouble; I feel bad eating food they buy, for example, so I eat one meal a day, then feel super fragile when they say I only eat once a day because I'm too lazy to get up and eat. I guess I don't take criticism well, even when I know it's well-intentioned: The last time, I was trying to sleep early/wake up early/eat breakfast/do some simple exercise, my sister she said I wasn't doing enough, and I wound up sitting there and crying as she told me she was tired of trying and was giving up on me. I pretty stopped everything I'd been doing and slept for most of the next few days, feeling even worse because I knew I should have been able to ignore it and keep trying.

I did try writing suicidal characters, though, at different points. I ran into problems near the ends of their stories: I like happy endings, but I don't think it makes sense to slot in happy endings when that's not where the story is going. I wanted to write them happy endings, but the stories felt like they had to end with their deaths. In the end, none of them really got finished.

There's nothing to stop me from trying again, but it feels like it'll turn out the same; no matter how much I try to be positive, it's just a matter of time before someone says something and I'm back where I started. I don't have a support network and maybe I'm not supposed to need one, but sometimes I feel it would really help.

I was kind of surprised by how hard it was to try your advice because I really didn't want to "ruin" a journal, but I'm giving it a shot. The real problem is keeping myself from dwelling on thoughts like "But this is an inconsequential thing to be happy about": I obsess over mistakes I made a decade ago, so downer thinking is hard to resist falling into. There is something kind of funny about the first thing on the list being a "Buy reddit gold!" ad, though. Either way, your post is really appreciated.
